name: Cariay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; attested only by a von Martius 1867 wordlist (per Glottolog); no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: pt.wikipedia 'Língua cariaí' (wikitext), citing Ramirez 2019 (preprint) / 2020 for a Natterer 1831 Cariaí vocabulary of ~70 items.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the Natterer forms are given in Ramirez's transcription with three final-accented items (weú, tʃebé, dewé) and no rule.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page cari1280 (Cariay) with its three references (Ramirez 2001, Ramirez 2020, Martius 1867).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; classifies Cariay as an independent Northern Arawakan (Negro-Roraima) language, extinct, 'preserved only in a wordlist by von Martius 1867'.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: EDUA. xi+796 pp. Section 8.2 'Os Cariaí, os Manao, os Wirina e os Aruã', pp. 517-524; Cariaí column in the 47-language comparative list, p. 564ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM5476 .R36 2001
sources.note: Nothing for Cariaí. Section 8.2 (pp. 517-524) only reproduces the Spix/Martius Cariaí wordlist beside Manao (Spix) and Wirina (Natterer), with the remark that 'temos pequenas listas de vocábulos reproduzidas em Martius (1863)'; no phonology, no accent statement. All 80 'acento' hits in the book belong to the Baniwa-Curripaco, Tariano, Warekena and Baré chapters (2.1.5, 3.1.5, 3.2.5, 4.3.10).

sources.citation: en.wikipedia 'Kariaí language' (stub): Kaufman 1994 placed it in a Manao branch, not followed by Aikhenvald 1999.

Martius, C. F. P. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, I: Zur Ethnographie. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Vergleichung von Jabaána-Wörtern', pp. 628-629 (Cariay items).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: A dozen Cariay body-part and nature words in a comparative list; ethnographic remarks on the Cariay as a Manao-league horde; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1863 [1867]. Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium / Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen (Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II). Leipzig: Fleischer. Cariay wordlist pp. 231-232 ('Von Spix in Carvoeiro, am Rio Negro, aufgezeichnet'); orthographic preface p. 29.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a ~170-item Latin-Cariay wordlist (Spix, Carvoeiro) with sporadic acute/circumflex marks (e.g. amalschyàny, uamàra patu, aurêma-auynoa, nutukunêta, ghuputuána, nulúla). The volume-wide preface (p. 29) says the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' and the circumflex gives o/u a 'dumpferen Laut' — so the marks are ambiguous between vowel quality and stress; there is no statement about Cariay stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados, vol. II (pp. 413-620; Cariay pp. 539-574). Curitiba: Editora CRV. ISBN 9786555788921 (print) / 9786555788938 (digital).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only modern treatment of Cariay (Glottolog's named source): reanalyses Spix's and Natterer's wordlists, classifies the language, and may offer a phonological interpretation of the accent marks; the sole place a stress remark could exist.

sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1831. Manuscript Cariaí (Carahiahy) vocabulary collected on the Pamonönü/Unini near Carvoeiro, Rio Negro (Natterer wordlist collection, Basel/Vienna), as edited in Ramirez 2020.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second and larger independent primary record of the language; Natterer's lists often carry accent marks, so it is the only other possible evidence of Cariay stress placement.

sources.citation: Ferreira, [first name not seen]. 2017. Sistemas fonológicos das línguas Arawak: um estudo tipológico. MA dissertation, Unicamp. DOI 10.47749/t/unicamp.2017.988227.
